stem: If (mx²+3x+4)/(x²+2x+2)<5 for every real x, then m satisfies
answer: Exact condition m<71/24; choices B and D both follow
solution: The denominator (x+1)²+1 is positive. The condition is (m−5)x²−7x−6<0 for all x. It requires m−5<0 and discriminant 49+24(m−5)<0, equivalently m<71/24. This implies both B and the weaker disjunction D, so the alternatives are not mutually exclusive.
hint: Reduce to a quadratic that must stay strictly negative.
notes: The likely intended necessary condition is B, but D is also a necessary consequence. No unique literal answer.

stem: How many solutions satisfy x+y=2, y+z=2, 2x+3y+z=6?
options: More than one but finitely many
solution: Twice the first equation plus the second is precisely the third. Letting y=t gives x=z=2−t for arbitrary real t.
hint: Check whether one equation is dependent on the others.
notes: The third right-hand side is 6, checked in a magnified crop.

stem: Let f(x)=det([[cos x,x,1],[2sin x,x²,2x],[tan x,x,1]]). Find limₓ→₀f(x)/x².
solution: Subtract the third row from the first. Expanding along the resulting row gives f(x)=(cosx−tanx)(x²−2x²)=x²(tanx−cosx). The quotient tends to −1.
hint: Subtract the two rows that share their last entries.

stem: What value must be assigned to f(x)=[1−cos(7(x−π))]/(x−π) at x=π to make f continuous?
solution: Put h=x−π. Since 1−cos7h=O(h²), the quotient is O(h) and tends to zero.
hint: Use 1−cosu≈u²/2 near zero.

stem: The real solutions of x²+4|x|−4=0 are
solution: For t=|x|≥0, t²+4t−4=0 gives t=−2+√8; the other quadratic root is negative and inadmissible. Hence x=±(√8−2).
hint: Solve for |x| first.
notes: The source’s last alternative prints −2±8 without a visible radical; preserved as printed.

stem: The roots of x³−9x²+23x−15=0 are in A.P. Their common difference is
answer: 2 when the roots are ordered increasingly
solution: The cubic factors as (x−1)(x−3)(x−5). Thus the increasing roots are 1,3,5 with common difference 2.
hint: The middle root of three arithmetic-progression roots equals their average.

stem: If a₁,a₂,… are in G.P., find Δ=det([[log aₙ,log aₙ₊₁,log aₙ₊₂],[log aₙ₊₃,log aₙ₊₄,log aₙ₊₅],[log aₙ₊₆,log aₙ₊₇,log aₙ₊₈]]).
answer: Δ=0, but A, B and C all have this value
solution: For positive G.P. terms, log aₖ=A+(k−1)d. The three rows differ by constant multiples of (1,1,1), so their determinant is zero. Also aₙaₙ₊₈=aₙ₊₄² and a₁a₃=a₂², making both alternatives A and B zero as well.
hint: Logarithms convert a geometric progression to an arithmetic progression.
notes: The alternatives A,B,C overlap exactly; all are zero. Positive terms are implicit in the real logarithms.

stem: Let f(x)=x for 0<x<1; f(x)=2−x for 1<x≤2; and f(x)=x−x²/2 for x>2. Then f is
options: Continuous at 2 but not differentiable at 1
Not continuous at 2 and not differentiable at 1
answer: The source leaves f(1) undefined; intended continuous extension has a kink there
solution: At 2 the middle value is zero and the right limit is 2−2=0, so f is continuous there. Neither of the first two branches includes 1, so differentiability at 1 is formally not defined. If one fills f(1)=1, the left and right slopes are 1 and −1, giving the intended first choice.
hint: Check whether each joining point belongs to the displayed domain.
notes: Both source inequalities at x=1 are strict. Missing f(1) is retained rather than silently supplied.

stem: Find limₓ→₀[1/x−log(1+x)/x²].
solution: The expression is [x−ln(1+x)]/x². Using ln(1+x)=x−x²/2+O(x³) gives limit 1/2.
hint: Use the second-order logarithm expansion.

stem: For |a|<1, |b|<1, the series a(a+b)+a²(a²+b²)+a³(a³+b³)+⋯
solution: The nth summand is a²ⁿ+(ab)ⁿ. Both are convergent geometric series because |a²|<1 and |ab|<1. Sum them separately.
hint: Separate the two geometric series.

stem: If a+1/a=2cosα, then aⁿ+1/aⁿ equals
solution: The equation a²−2cosα·a+1=0 has roots e^(±iα). Taking integer nth powers and adding reciprocals gives e^(inα)+e^(−inα)=2cos(nα).
hint: Use the quadratic equation for a or the cosine recurrence.

stem: For positive a,b,c, the least value of (a+b+c)(1/a+1/b+1/c) is
solution: Cauchy–Schwarz gives (a+b+c)(1/a+1/b+1/c)≥(1+1+1)²=9. Equality occurs at a=b=c.
hint: Apply Cauchy–Schwarz.

stem: Define f(x)=|x|−[x]−1 for −1<x<0; |x|−[x] for 0≤x<1; and 1 otherwise. The source defines [x] as the greatest integer strictly less than x. Then
options: f is discontinuous at only one real point
f is discontinuous at more than one real point
f is continuous but nondifferentiable at only one real point
answer: Literal strict-integer definition gives one discontinuity; conventional floor gives a different answer
solution: With the printed strict definition, [0]=−1. For −1<x<0, f=−x; for 0<x<1, f=x; and f(0)=1. Thus only 0 is discontinuous, giving A. With the conventional greatest-integer function floor(x), f(0)=0 and f=min{|x|,1}, continuous with three nondifferentiable points −1,0,1, giving D. The intended convention needs clarification.
hint: Evaluate the integer-part symbol at the integer 0.
notes: Source uses “greatest integer <x”, conflicting with conventional floor notation. Conditional answers are given without silently correcting the definition.

stem: If a primal linear program has feasible solutions but no optimal solution, then its dual
options: Has feasible solutions but no optimal solution
solution: A feasible finite-dimensional linear program without an optimum is unbounded in the optimizing direction. A feasible dual would supply a finite bound by weak duality, which is impossible.
hint: Use weak duality to rule out dual feasibility.

stem: Maximize 2x₁+3x₂ subject to 2x₁+x₂>2, x₁+x₂≤3, x₁−x₂≤−1 and x₁,x₂>0. Which is true?
answer: No attained optimum under the printed strict positivity constraints
solution: The objective is 3(x₁+x₂)−x₁≤9−x₁<9 since x₁>0. For arbitrarily small ε>0, (ε,3−ε) is feasible and has value 9−ε→9. Thus the supremum is 9 but it is not attained.
hint: Distinguish strict positivity from nonnegativity.
notes: Magnification confirms > in the first and nonnegativity lines, while the other two use ≤. If the intended final constraint were ≥0, choice A would instead be optimal.

stem: Evaluate ∫₋₁¹(x+x²+x³)e^(−x²/2)dx.
answer: None of the printed values matches the integral
solution: The odd x and x³ terms integrate to zero, leaving ∫₋₁¹x²e^(−x²/2)dx>0. Integration by parts gives −2/√e+∫₋₁¹e^(−x²/2)dx≈0.498187. This is neither 2/√e≈1.213061 nor 2√e≈3.297443, and cannot be negative.
hint: Use parity before evaluating the remaining even integral.
notes: The printed integrand reads x+x²+x³, so the provided alternatives appear inconsistent; no official key supplied.

stem: The series Σₙ₌₁^∞(−1)ⁿ⁺¹/n
solution: Alternating decreasing terms 1/n tend to zero, so the alternating-series test gives convergence. Absolute values give the divergent harmonic series. Integrating the geometric expansion of 1/(1+x) on [0,1] gives the sum ln2.
hint: Apply the alternating-series test and identify the logarithm series.
